specification.title: A nested scope fails, and its ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT fails on the client
steps: Start the outer transaction with the framework's ordinary transaction API, on a pool of one connection.
Write the marker `outer`, and make sure the write was sent.
Start a nested scope with the framework's nested-transaction (savepoint) API. Write the marker `inner` in it, and make sure the write was sent.
Checkpoint `inner-after-write`: report the backend PID. The runner sees the savepoint's subtransaction lock.
Arm the client-side fault (the next ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT fails in the driver and is not sent), then raise an application error in the nested scope.
When the fault fires, before the framework sees its error, the adapter's driver layer reports checkpoint `after-fault` (the backend PID): the runner records the fault's effect on the server.
The outer scope catches the nested scope's error.
Checkpoint `after-outer`, after the outer transaction's API has returned: report the same backend PID. The runner records whether that session is still inside a transaction.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the API has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: If the API reports that the outer transaction committed, PostgreSQL committed it, with the outer scope's writes and none of the failed nested scope's writes.
When the outer transaction's API has returned, the connection that ran it is no longer inside a transaction.

execution.description: Declarative @Transactional on the same DataSourceTransactionManager and DriverManagerDataSource. The adapter calls a JDK proxy advised by TransactionInterceptor. It does not call the target directly. Nested work is a second call on that proxy, with PROPAGATION_NESTED or PROPAGATION_REQUIRES_NEW. The default rollback rule is RuntimeException and Error. TX-03.statement-error-rollback-not-sent is not in this mode. TX-05.explicit-serializable is not in this mode: @Transactional does not return a transaction handle.

configuration.rollbackRule: default RuntimeException and Error; TX-03.statement-error-rollback-not-sent uses rollbackFor Exception.class

execution.form: Declarative: the call goes through a JDK proxy and TransactionInterceptor. Outer PROPAGATION_REQUIRED. Inner PROPAGATION_NESTED, which DataSourceTransactionManager maps to a JDBC savepoint. Not PROPAGATION_REQUIRES_NEW.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

fault.mechanism: A client-side injection in the adapter's driver layer (node-postgres, pg.Client.prototype.query): ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT fails without being sent, as a failed send would.
fault.injection_point: The framework's rollback of the nested scope.
fault.preconditions: The framework's statements pass through the instrumented pg module (recorded as trace_sees_framework_pg).
fault.expected_server: The savepoint is never rolled back: the nested scope's write stays in the outer transaction.
fault.expected_client: An error from the nested scope's rollback; what the framework then does is under test.

knowledge: The framework knows that its savepoint rollback failed, so it knows that the nested scope's writes may still be in the transaction.

api_outcome.basis: the @Transactional proxy returned normally, so the interceptor committed
api_outcome.contract: Spring Framework 7.0.9 @Transactional methods run through TransactionInterceptor (org.springframework.transaction.interceptor.TransactionAspectSupport.completeTransactionAfterThrowing). The call is on a JDK proxy. The target is not invoked directly. If TransactionAttribute.rollbackOn returns true, the interceptor calls PlatformTransactionManager.rollback and rethrows the application throwable. If rollback throws TransactionSystemException, that exception replaces the application throwable and initApplicationException stores the original. If rollbackOn returns false, the interceptor calls commit. With no rollbackFor rules, RuleBasedTransactionAttribute.rollbackOn delegates to DefaultTransactionAttribute.rollbackOn, which is true for RuntimeException and Error only. The 7.0.9 reference, Rolling Back a Declarative Transaction, states: "In its default configuration, the Spring Framework's transaction infrastructure code marks a transaction for rollback only in the case of runtime, unchecked exceptions. That is, when the thrown exception is an instance or subclass of RuntimeException. (Error instances also, by default, result in a rollback)." A normal return is reported as committed. The method's own throwable leaving the proxy is reported as rolled_back. Any other throwable leaving the proxy is reported as failed. Propagation.NESTED, Spring Framework 7.0.9: "Execute within a nested transaction if a current transaction exists, behave like REQUIRED otherwise." DataSourceTransactionManager's class javadoc says nestedTransactionAllowed defaults to true and nested transactions use JDBC savepoints. Propagation.REQUIRES_NEW: "Create a new transaction, and suspend the current transaction if one exists." The statement-error case uses rollbackFor = Exception.class so a checked SQLException takes the rollback path that case describes. The default rule would commit on that checked exception. That default is not substituted for the case.

error.message: Could not roll back to JDBC savepoint: application error: the nested scope fails: injected client-side failure: ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT was not sent

evaluation.reason: TX-02.1 violated: the API reported: committed; xid 9416 committed at report time (`after-outer`); outer visible: true; inner (failed scope) visible: true

preconditions.description: the write of marker "outer" had reached PostgreSQL at `outer-after-write` (a row lock on item, in pg_locks)
the write of marker "inner" had reached PostgreSQL at `inner-after-write` (a subtransaction lock, in pg_locks)
the client-side fault (client-reject) fired exactly once
the nested scope's error reached the outer scope, which handled it
the runner observed the transaction's session after the outer API returned
the withheld ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT left the savepoint live: the session was in its transaction, holding the savepoint's subtransaction lock
preconditions.detail: at `after-fault`: session "idle in transaction", backend_xid 9416; transactionid locks [9416, 9417]
